Theme

Latin word

praesēns

praesēns, praesentis

adjective, third declension, one ending

present, current (as against past or future); immediate, instant; in person, face to face; present, in person; mē praesente, in my presence

In this lexicon

  • current

    the recommended word · classical · Gell. 1.10.4: loquere verbīs praesentibus, words now in use (Lewis & Short); Caes. BC 1.52: inopiā praesentis, sed etiam futūrī temporis (Lewis & Short)

  • immediate

    also used · classical · Cic. Div. 2.122: praesēns poena, instant punishment (Lewis & Short); Cic. Clu. 34: praesentī pecūniā, with ready money (Lewis & Short)

  • personal

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 2.7.4: praesēns tēcum ēgī; Cic. Att. 2.12.2: praesentem audīre mālō

  • presence

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 2.12.2: praesentem audīre mālō

  • pecūnia praesēns: cash

    classical

  • tempus praesēns: present tense

    late Latin

Examples

  • vīve ergō mōribus praeteritīs, loquere verbīs praesentibus

    live, then, by the ways of the past, but speak the words of the presentGell. 1.10.4

    In the entry for current

  • adnotābant seniōrēs, quibus ōtiōsum est vetera et praesentia contendere

    the older men, who have time to compare past and present, remarkedTac. Ann. 13.3

    In the entry for current

  • adsum praesēns praesentī tibi

    here I am, face to face with youPlaut. Ps. 5.1.27 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for presence

    To be face to face with you.Traupman 312
